title: Commitment signal multiplexer and safe throttle proxy
author: Priya Natarajan
description: Motivation: We see recurring incidents where autoscaler decisions diverge from external commitment inputs (billing/reservation overrides, SRE manual patches, and predictive headroom hints), causing transient overcommit or overly-conservative throttles. This PR introduces a Commitment Signal Multiplexer and a Safe Throttle Proxy to 1) consolidate multiple commitment sources into a single normalized commitment feed, 2) apply conservative safety rules and smoothing for downstream autoscalers and per-tenant throttle enforcement, and 3) provide observability for reconciliation reasoning. High-level changes: - pkg/autoscaler/commitment_mux: new multiplexer that ingests: reservation ledger commits, predictive headroom hints, manual overrides (Linear/console), and observed utilization signal. It publishes a time-series normalized_commitment{tenant} with provenance tags and confidence scores. Multiplexer implements configurable priority ordering, hysteresis windows, and a small Bayesian smoothing step to avoid flips on noisy signals. - pkg/throttle/proxy: safe-throttle-proxy sits in front of the per-tenant throttle gate. It consumes normalized_commitment and will (a) clamp outgoing throttle budgets if observed instantaneous QPS would violate commitment+headroom, (b) emit a soft-fallback token path that falls back to lower-cost model variants when capacity tight, and (c) surface a recommended autoscaler_adjustment suggestion via the autoscaler API. - Telemetry: new metrics (redwood_commitment_normalized, redwood_commitment_adjustments_total, redwood_throttle_clamps, redwood_throttle_suggested_adjustments) and an events stream for mismatch reasons. - Config/ops: feature gate enable_commitment_mux (off by default), per-tenant policy overrides with allowlist/denylist, and a rollout plan with canary-only for reserved pools. - Backward compatibility: when the feature is off, autoscaler reads remain unchanged. Multiplexer mode supports a passthrough profile to mirror existing behavior for rollout. - Testing: unit tests for mux priority/hysteresis, integration e2e that replays reservation ledger events and predictive hints, and smoke test for the safe-throttle proxy with synthetic bursts. - Migration: small DB migration to add provenance columns to the reservation ledger (safely backfilled), and a short-lived compatibility shim for older controllers. The description below enumerates the diff surface, CI outcome, and review thread. Overall risk: medium; runtime changes touch the hot path for throttle decisions but are guarded behind a feature gate and incremental canary rollout. Rollout plan: enable in canary reserved pool for 48h -> expand to 10% of dedicated capacity -> full rollout with monitoring checks for throttle clamp rates and autoscaler churn.

review_discussion: Ethan Liao: Overall direction LGTM. A couple of questions: 1) Can you clarify the smoothing window math? The unit tests show 5s but comments say 30s. 2) Is the DB migration safe for clusters with large ledgers?

Priya Natarajan: Good catch on the comment mismatch — smoothing window is configurable and default is 30s; updated tests to explicitly set small window for unit tests. For DB migration we do a 'create column null' then backfill in a background job; details in migration SQL comments.

Marisa Ortega: The proxy looks like it could add extra latency on edge paths. Have you benchmarked p99 added latency? We should gate it behind the feature flag and add a latency budget threshold in the canary rollout.
Priya Natarajan: Added a microbench in pkg/throttle/proxy/bench_test.go; p99 added ~0.7ms in our local perf harness. We'll use the canary gate and an alert to auto-rollback if p99 > 2ms.
Liam Gardner: Testing looks thorough. Suggest adding an alert for 'commitment_adjustments_total > X' to catch noisy signal storms; otherwise approve once docs/ops checklist included.
Priya Natarajan: Added alert suggestion and operator runbook. Thank you for the review — addressing final nits now.
CI Bot: unit-tests failed on first run (race detected in multiplexer subscriber list).
Priya Natarajan: Fixed race by switching to copy-on-write subscriber updates and re-ran tests.
Marisa Ortega: Approve (docs + runbook look good).

release_notes: Introduce Commitment Signal Multiplexer (experimental, feature-gated) and Safe Throttle Proxy to consolidate commitment inputs and prevent overcommit. Add telemetry for commitment adjustments and throttle clamps. Off by default; ops runbook included for canary rollout.
